First, a quick question — what kind of application process are you working with?
🎓

Regular Schools

Everything else — Common App, Coalition App, or a school's own application. This covers the vast majority of colleges, including arts & portfolio schools.

🎖️

Service Academies

West Point, the Naval Academy, the Air Force Academy, and the Coast Guard Academy — a genuinely different process: congressional nomination, medical exam, fitness test, and a service commitment after graduation.

Not sure, or applying to a mix of both? Pick "Regular Schools" — you can switch anytime from the dashboard, and nothing here locks you out of any school.

Quick Tour

Here's what's inside Compass

A quick rundown before you dive in — you can always come back to any of this later.
🔎 Explore Yourself
Get to Know Yourself — a private self-reflection quiz. Nothing here gets sent anywhere, it's just for you.
Roadmap — a general grade-by-grade guide for what to focus on.
Major Finder — a short quiz to help narrow down what you might want to study.
🧱 Build Your Profile
My Activities — log your extracurriculars, jobs, and competitions.
My Grades — log your courses and grades for a rough GPA estimate.
Test Scores — log your SAT or ACT score.
My Application Data — saves everything you write across Compass into one place, and lets you print or copy it all as a summary.
🎯 Find & Apply
Find My College — answer a short survey and get a ranked list of real matches from Compass's data.
College Data — a searchable database of real schools with real numbers.
Dream Schools — your actual shortlist, with deadlines, status, and essay prompts per school.
Planner & Deadlines — every deadline in one place, plus recommendation letters, scholarships, and financial aid reminders.
Essays & Notes — a roomy space to actually write and revise every essay you owe.

Planner & Deadlines

✍️ Your Input
Everything time-sensitive, in one place.
💵 Financial aid deadlines — separate from admission deadlines
FAFSA opens every year on October 1 for the following school year — this is the same nationwide, regardless of which schools you're applying to. Submit it as early as you reasonably can; some aid is first-come, first-served.

CSS Profile (required by many private schools in addition to FAFSA) has its own deadline set by each individual school — and it's sometimes earlier than that school's actual admission deadline. Compass doesn't have per-school CSS Profile dates yet, so check each school's own financial aid page directly, especially for any private schools on your list.

Essays & Notes

A roomier space to actually write and revise — everything here is the same data as your Dream Schools page, just easier to work in.
📝 Personal Statement / Main Essay
Most applications (like the Common App) use one main essay across every school. Common topic categories: your background or identity, a challenge you overcame, a belief that was challenged, something you're grateful for, an accomplishment, or a topic of your choice.

🎯 Find & Apply ✍️ Category tags are yours
Search by college name, major, or interest
Type an exact school name (e.g. "Harvard") to jump straight to it, or search broadly by major or type of school (e.g. "computer science," "liberal arts," "public").
Figures are recent published admissions data (Common Data Set / class-profile releases) for enrolled first-year classes, rounded to the nearest reporting cycle. Acceptance rates, score ranges, and cost figures shift year to year — costs shown are rough sticker-price estimates before any financial aid or scholarships, not what most families actually pay. Treat all of this as a general compass, not a cutoff, and confirm current figures on each school's admissions and financial aid pages before you apply.

About the "Show deadlines, grad rate & more" details: those six fields (deadlines, grad rate, student:faculty ratio, average net price, merit scholarships, demonstrated interest) are estimated by school category — elite need-blind privates, public flagships, conservatories, service academies, and other privates each get the same typical range — not looked up individually per school. Treat them as a rough starting expectation, and always verify the real numbers on the school's own site before relying on them.
This tool reflects general, publicly known patterns in U.S. college admissions and is for personal planning only — it doesn't predict or guarantee any outcome. Requirements vary a lot by school, program, and year, especially for athletic recruiting (NCAA/NAIA eligibility rules) and arts portfolios/auditions, so always confirm specifics with a school counselor, coach, or the college's own admissions office.
